newsitem.title: FINLAND: PK CABLES SAYS BRAZIL PROJECT ON TRACK.
newsitem.headline: PK CABLES SAYS BRAZIL PROJECT ON TRACK.

text.p: Finnish industrial wiring group PK Cables Oy's plans start manufacturing in Brazil are on track for start-up in the autumn, and the group may soon announce a local partner, CEO Tom Hakalax said on Friday.

"The Brazil project is under way. We have established a company there, and production will begin at the end of this year," Hakalax told Reuters in an interview at the plant in northern Finland, near Oulu.
The company had been in talks with four prospective partners and talks with one had progressed to a stage where there could be a deal soon.

"It looks good, but we're just now putting things on paper...It will probably be clear in May whether something is going to come of this, Hakalax said, adding, however, that the project itself did not depend on finding a partner.
"Our own plans will go ahead regardless," he said.
Finnish venture capital fund, Finnfund was also likely to join the project, he said.

PK Cables has said it will set up a production unit near the town of Curitaba in Brazil that would produce wiring for the heavy vehicle industry and would initially have annual sales of about 40 million markka.
The company's main customers, Swedish truck makers Scania and Volvo Trucks , both have production units in Brazil, and PK Cables, as their subcontractor, is following them abroad.
To begin with, the new Brazil unit would produce cable harnesses for Scania, but the company also hopes to serve Volvo there, Hakalax said.
For the time being the group had no concrete plans to establish itself elsewhere, Hakalax said: "Brazil is what we are doing now."
But PK Cables was keeping its eyes open for opportunities elsewhere, too, in emerging markets, he said.
